On today's conference call, Tim Cook discussed Apple's increasingly severe memory supply and pricing challenges, but hinted that adding more suppliers may not bring product prices back down. Details below.

「Pricing remains unclear」

Apple is seeking ways to alleviate the pressure of being forced to raise prices on multiple products due to the memory shortage, and has been lobbying the US government both publicly and privately to approve purchases of memory from Chinese suppliers ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) and Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), which are on the entity list.

On today's Q3 2026 earnings conference call, Tim Cook and Apple CFO Kevan Parekh were asked whether Apple's push to diversify its memory supply was 「about ensuring supply and easing memory inflation, or more about maintaining its value proposition for customers.」

After describing the dramatic rise in Apple's memory costs over the past several quarters, Cook said that adding suppliers would help improve supply stability, but warned that doing so may not allow Apple to reverse its recent product price increases:

Notably, Cook initially hinted that adding suppliers might help bring prices down, then specifically corrected himself, seemingly in an effort to lower expectations.

It is worth mentioning that Apple reportedly plans to use memory from Chinese suppliers in devices sold outside the US. Even so, this is still expected to allow Apple to reserve components from existing suppliers for products sold in the US market, thereby improving supply for both domestic and overseas devices.

In any case, Cook's repeated revisions of what 「adding suppliers」 actually means for Apple and its customers make it clear that the recent (and perhaps future) price increases are unlikely to be temporary measures, as many customers had hoped.
